_WARNING: THESE ARE EXAMPLE CAPS, NOT A SAFE DEFAULT FOR YOUR CHIP. Silicon degradation differs per CPU: on yours these numbers may be needlessly slow, or NOT LOW ENOUGH to protect you. Run Calibrate.ps1 to find YOUR chip's safe cap; it rewrites this file with your values. Until then the GUI's '[OK]' only means a cap was applied, not that it is correct for your silicon.
Note: Bundled profile values are EXAMPLES - run Calibrate.ps1 to set your own. Fields: PCoreMHz / ECoreMHz are caps in MHz (0 = no cap); PMaxStatePct / EMaxStatePct are max processor state % (99 = turbo off). The P-core cap lands roughly 100-130 MHz below the requested value in practice.

LowLoad.Description: Highest cap. P-core peak ~4.89 GHz (-13% single-thread vs stock; all-core unchanged), E-cores uncapped (~4.06 GHz). ~510 MHz below the highest passing point, ~720 MHz below the failure point. Use after 2+ clean weeks on Productivity.

Productivity.Description: Default daily driver. P-core peak ~4.48 GHz (-20% burst single-thread; sustained single-thread was already thermally limited to ~4.5 GHz, all-core unchanged), E-cores uncapped. ~920 MHz below the highest passing point.

Sustained.Description: Lowest frequency caps, for long all-core loads, heat and noise: all-core ~79 W / 85 C instead of ~101 W / 95 C, for about -7.5% all-core throughput. Also the first step-down after instability on Productivity.

TurboOff.Description: Turbo disabled on both core types: P ~2.14 GHz, E ~2.19 GHz, all-core ~55 W. Last-resort fallback.

Stock.Description: No limits. Reference only: fails the LP0 test at 5.6 GHz. Not recommended on this CPU.
